findings.issue: Unspecified issue.
findings.recommendation: Remediation not specified by the reviewer; requires architect input.

findings.issue: The remote access gateway in the DMZ brokers RDP sessions to engineering workstations without a hardened jump host, violating [network-management-standard.md §4.2].
findings.recommendation: Implement a hardened jump host with session recording for all interactive administrative sessions.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The gateway brokers each session with credentials held in its vault, so vendors never learn workstation passwords.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Logging, Monitoring & Detection
findings.issue: The remote access gateway does not forward logs to the central SIEM in near real time, violating [logging-detection-standard.md §2.1] Central aggregation.
findings.recommendation: Forward logs from the remote access gateway to the central SIEM in near real time.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The remote access gateway records every session as video with keystroke logs and keeps the recordings for 12 months.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Resilience, Backup & Incident Response
findings.issue: The design describes backups without immutability, offline copy, or a tested restore, violating [vulnerability-resilience-standard.md §4.2, §4.3, §4.4].
findings.recommendation: Implement immutability, offline copies, and regular restore testing.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Nightly backups of the site historian, OT domain controllers, engineering workstations and all PLC and HMI projects are written to the backup NAS in Level 3, and a weekly copy is written to encrypted removable disks that are disconnected and stored in the site safe.

findings.issue: The design places presentation, application and data tiers in the same zone, violating [segmentation-standard.md §2.1].
findings.recommendation: Place presentation, application and data tiers in separate zones, and state the trust relationship between zones.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Each production line has its own Level 2 switch stack, uplinked to the Level 3 core switches in the plant server room.

findings.issue: The Layer 3 boundary does not sit at the distribution layer in campus designs, violating [three-tier-lan-standard.md §2.2].
findings.recommendation: Move the Layer 3 boundary to the distribution layer in campus designs.
findings.evidence_excerpt: A pair of IT/OT firewalls separates the corporate LAN from the DMZ, and a second pair of OT firewalls separates the DMZ from Level 3.

findings.issue: Administrators connect to production from general-purpose workstations.
findings.recommendation: Implement a privileged access management solution with session recording, or use dedicated privileged access workstations.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The corporate group Controls-Engineers is a member of the OT-Admins group, which has local administrator rights on all Level 2 and Level 3 Windows hosts.

findings.issue: The OT Active Directory domain trusts the corporate domain through a one-way trust, which may create an exploitable path for lateral movement.
findings.recommendation: Implement a two-way trust or a separate, isolated OT domain.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The OT Active Directory domain (ot.brennock.local) trusts the corporate domain through a one-way trust, so that controls engineers log on to OT systems with their corporate accounts.

findings.issue: Inter-zone traffic is routed without a stateful inspection point between Level 2 VLANs 210-213 and Level 1 VLANs 110-112.
findings.recommendation: Implement a stateful inspection point between Level 2 VLANs 210-213 and Level 1 VLANs 110-112.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The Level 3 core switches route between Level 2 VLANs 210-213 and Level 1 VLANs 110-112 without access control lists.

findings.issue: The corporate SSID CAL-SCAN uses a pre-shared key, violating [network-management-standard.md §6.1] Wireless authentication.
findings.recommendation: Replace WPA2-Personal with WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X and EAP-TLS, and configure 802.1X authentication on the core switches.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The scanners connect to the SSID CAL-SCAN using WPA2-Personal with a single pre-shared key, and the SSID is bridged to VLAN 213 on the Level 3 core switches.

findings.issue: The use of pre-shared keys for corporate SSIDs requires client isolation and a segment boundary, which is not described.
findings.recommendation: Implement client isolation and a segment boundary for the CAL-SCAN SSID.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The warehouse supervisor loads the key onto each scanner at enrolment.

findings.section: Calderwick Plant IT/OT Network Architecture - High-Level Design
findings.issue: Unspecified issue.
findings.recommendation: Remediation not specified by the reviewer; requires architect input.

findings.issue: The network architecture allows administrators to connect to production from general-purpose workstations, violating [identity-access-standard.md §4.3]. This contradicts the security model, which assumes a secure identity and access management system.
findings.recommendation: Restrict administrators to connect to production only from designated, hardened workstations.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The OT Active Directory domain trusts the corporate domain through a one-way trust, which may create an exploitable path for lateral movement.

findings.issue: The network design places presentation, application and data tiers in the same zone, violating [segmentation-standard.md §2.1]. This contradicts the application architecture, which assumes network segmentation for tenant isolation.
findings.recommendation: Segregate presentation, application and data tiers into separate zones.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The design places presentation, application and data tiers in the same zone, violating [segmentation-standard.md §2.1].

findings.recommendation: Hold at least one immutable or air-gapped copy outside the production identity domain, and test restore at defined intervals with the result recorded against the stated RTO/RPO.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Logging, Monitoring & Detection
findings.issue: The design does not log data export or bulk read operations above a defined threshold, violating [logging-detection-standard.md §2.2] Mandatory event set.
findings.recommendation: Implement logging for data export or bulk read operations above a defined threshold.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The SOC has alert rules for failed logons, new local administrator accounts, firewall rule changes and blocked connection attempts from the DMZ.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Vulnerability & Patch Management
findings.issue: The design does not describe how patching is performed without an outage, as required by [vulnerability-resilience-standard.md §3.2].
findings.recommendation: Describe the maintenance approach for patching in the design document.
findings.evidence_excerpt: They run application allowlisting in enforce mode and antivirus, and USB mass storage is disabled by device control policy.

findings.issue: The design does not assign each workload to a named security zone, violating [segmentation-standard.md §2.1].
findings.recommendation: Assign each workload to a named security zone, and state the trust relationship between zones.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The network follows the Purdue reference model, summarised in Table 1.

findings.issue: Privileged MFA relies on FIDO2 security keys, which are acceptable, but the use of FIDO2 for non-privileged access is not explicitly stated.
findings.recommendation: Mandate MFA for all interactive access to enterprise systems, including non-privileged access.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Every session through the remote access gateway requires a FIDO2 security key and ends automatically after four hours; vendor sessions must also be approved in the gateway by the on-shift production supervisor.

findings.issue: The design does not constrain server-to-server traffic within the DMZ zone, violating [segmentation-standard.md §3.2].
findings.recommendation: Implement micro-segmentation within the DMZ zone to constrain server-to-server traffic.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The DMZ is the only zone to which both corporate and plant systems may connect.

findings.issue: Controller key switches are left in the REMOTE position, allowing unauthorised access to the control system.
findings.recommendation: Ensure controller key switches are in the LOCAL position when not in use.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Controller key switches on all lines are left in the REMOTE position so that logic changes can be downloaded from the engineering workstations without an electrician attending the cabinet.

findings.issue: Line HMIs start automatically at boot and log on with the local Windows account hmi-operator, potentially allowing unauthorised access.
findings.recommendation: Implement additional authentication and authorisation controls for Line HMIs.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Line HMIs start automatically at boot and log on with the local Windows account hmi-operator, so that operator screens are available immediately after a power cycle.

findings.issue: Unused access ports are left enabled in the control VLAN, allowing unauthorised access.
findings.recommendation: Disable unused access ports in the control VLAN.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Unused access ports on the Level 1 and Level 2 switches are left enabled in the line's control VLAN so that maintenance contractors can connect laptops for drive tuning without raising a change request.

findings.issue: The engineering workstations (EWS-01 to EWS-04) are not constrained by micro-segmentation, violating [segmentation-standard.md §3.2].
findings.recommendation: Implement micro-segmentation for the engineering workstations (EWS-01 to EWS-04) to constrain server-to-server traffic within the zone.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Four engineering workstations (EWS-01 to EWS-04) hold the controller, robot and HMI engineering software and are the only hosts from which logic is downloaded to controllers.

findings.issue: The application architecture assumes network segmentation for tenant isolation, but the network design has one flat segment.
findings.recommendation: Implement network segmentation for tenant isolation.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Approved equipment vendors connect from the internet to the remote access gateway in the DMZ and open RDP sessions to the engineering workstations in Level 3. The gateway brokers each session with credentials held in its vault, so vendors never learn workstation IP addresses or credentials.

findings.issue: The design does not describe how data moves between components. Without a data flow, encryption-in-transit, boundary controls and data residency cannot be assessed at all - their absence from the findings below means they were unreviewable, not that they are sound.
findings.recommendation: Add a data flow diagram or a flow table listing, for each flow: source, destination, protocol, and what data it carries.

findings.issue: The design does not classify the data it handles. Retention, residency, encryption strength and access-logging requirements all derive from classification, so none of them can be checked.
findings.recommendation: State, per data store and per flow, the classification of the data held or carried (for example Public / Internal / Confidential / PHI).

findings.issue: No threat model or documented attack-surface analysis accompanies the design.
findings.recommendation: Produce a STRIDE or equivalent threat model covering every trust boundary in the design, with mitigations traced to specific controls and residual risks accepted by a named owner.
